The second lane's prepare step runs "clearing runtime artifacts" + `rsync --delete` into that shared tree; if the first lane's job is RUNNING (not merely PENDING), the re-rsync can rip code/data out from under it mid-run. In the 2026-08-03 incident the second lane's re-rsync happened while job 19036499 was still PENDING (harmless — tree re-laid identically from main), but the RUNNING case is a live data-loss path. Suggested companion fix to the job-name threading: suffix the scratch dir with the same lane_suffix (`eps/issue-<N>-<lane_suffix>`), or refuse prepare when a RUNNING job already holds the tree.
